title: Binyamin the Shepherd
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Berakhot 40b: he ate bread and said, “Blessed is the Master of this bread,” and Rav said, “He has fulfilled his obligation.” In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:2, a certain Persian asked Rav about this. Hyman concludes that undoubtedly Binyamin the Shepherd was from the land of Persia.

notes.text: כרך ריפתא here means that he ate bread, as the William Davidson English Berakhot 40b also renders the accompanying Aramaic. The conclusion that Binyamin was Persian is Hyman’s inference from the separate Jerusalem Talmud account, not a new identity binding.
The fuller blessing in the consulted Bavli includes Rachmana. The Jerusalem Talmud describes the questioner as a Persian without giving his name.
